summary: Long-form essay reader paired with spaced-repetition flashcards: essays are ingested from an author-maintained markdown file into ordered sections, each section owns flashcards that link back to the passage that taught them, and a due-queue review loop schedules re-review using a deterministic interval algorithm.

classification.why_application: Owns the essaycards schema (essays, sections, flashcards, review state), owns the markdown ingestion grammar and upsert-by-stable-key semantics, and owns the spaced-repetition scheduling algorithm — all essay-content-specific and review-specific domain behavior, not reusable technical infrastructure.
non_goals: In-app authoring or editing UI for essay text or flashcards
Typed-answer grading (flip-and-self-assess only, not text matching)
Any ingestion path other than the markdown format defined in this document (no upload UI, no API-based import)
classification.not_platform: The markdown ingestion grammar, the essay/section/flashcard domain model, and the spaced-repetition scheduling formula are meaningful only within this application. No other Atlas application ingests essay content or schedules flashcard review; nothing here is a generic reusable primitive.

consumes: Shared Atlas Postgres instance (02_Platform/Postgres) — connection via ATLAS_PG_* or DATABASE_URL env vars
platform_errorhandling — api_error helper, exception handlers, request timing, structured logging
A markdown source file provided by the user on the local filesystem, mounted into the container for the ingestion CLI to read (no HTTP upload path exists)
provides: GET /api/essaycards/essays — list all ingested essays; no params; returns Dataset ordered by created_at asc
GET /api/essaycards/essays/{essay_id} — single essay with its ordered sections embedded; returns Dataset (single row); 404 ApiError if not found
GET /api/essaycards/flashcards/due — due flashcards, optionally scoped to an essay or a section within an essay; returns Dataset ordered by next_due_at asc
POST /api/essaycards/flashcards/{flashcard_id}/review — grade a card and persist its next scheduling state; mutation endpoint, returns typed record on success
invariants: All read endpoints (GET) return Dataset per R-CON-BP-04
essays.slug is unique; essay_sections.(essay_id, anchor_slug) is unique; flashcards.(essay_id, card_key) is unique — these are exactly the three upsert keys defined by the ingestion contract
anchor_slug is always author-assigned from the source file's `{#slug}` heading suffix — the parser never derives an anchor from heading text
card_key is always the author-assigned id from the source file (e.g. fc-origins-1) — the parser never generates ids
Re-ingestion of an existing flashcard (matched by card_key) updates question, answer, and section_id only; flashcard_review_state.last_reviewed_at and next_due_at are never modified by re-ingestion
A newly ingested flashcard (no prior row with that card_key) gets flashcard_review_state.last_reviewed_at = null and next_due_at = the flashcard row's created_at, making it due immediately

Ingestion is fully transactional: parsing and validation happen entirely before any database write; if any validation error occurs anywhere in the file, no rows are inserted or updated for that ingestion run
'Due' is defined as next_due_at <= now(), where now() is evaluated by Postgres at query time (single time-authority; see R-CON-AL-06 note below)
The four grade values are exactly: again, hard, good, easy — no other value is accepted

POST .../review reads and validates the request body manually against the raw parsed JSON (grade must be present and be a string in {again, hard, good, easy}) instead of relying on a Pydantic-enforced required field. Every invalid-body shape — missing grade, non-string grade, out-of-set grade, or an unparsable JSON body — is caught by application code and returned as ApiError with error.code=VALIDATION_ERROR (400); FastAPI's default RequestValidationError 422 shape is never produced by this endpoint, per R-CON-BP-04
Grading always sets last_reviewed_at to the request-handling instant, for every grade including again
For grade=again: next_due_at = now + 5 seconds, flat — the floor/doubling formula does not apply to again

For grade in {hard, good, easy}: floor is 1 minute / 20 minutes / 1 day respectively; elapsed = null if last_reviewed_at was null else (now - last_reviewed_at); interval = floor if elapsed is null else max(floor, 2 * elapsed); next_due_at = now + interval

R-CON-AL-06 time authority: the single authoritative 'now' for a review request is read once from Postgres (`select now()`) at the start of the review transaction, then reused as both the persisted last_reviewed_at value and the base for computing next_due_at — the client never sends a timestamp and the app server's local clock is never used, avoiding drift between the due-boundary check and the scheduling arithmetic

R-CON-AL-04/05 (partial update / null-vs-omit semantics) do not apply to this component: there are no PATCH or partial-update endpoints. The only mutation endpoint (POST .../review) takes one required field (grade) with no nullable/omittable fields and no partial-update meaning
Section body_markdown excludes the trailing flashcards fence — see 'Markdown ingestion grammar' below for the exact extraction rule

Content appearing in the source file before the first `##` section heading is discarded — there is no essay-level intro/body field in this schema; only sections carry markdown content. This is an explicit design decision (not a bug) — see risks.
If GET /flashcards/due is called with section_id set and essay_id omitted, this is rejected as VALIDATION_ERROR (section_id requires essay_id, per the draft's stated allowed combinations)

If GET /flashcards/due is called with an essay_id/section_id combination where the section does not actually belong to that essay, the query returns zero rows (not an error) — the WHERE clause ANDs both filters against the flashcard row's own essay_id and section_id columns
failure_modes: VALIDATION_ERROR — POST .../review with a grade outside {again, hard, good, easy}, including a missing grade field, a non-string grade value, or an unparsable JSON body (all validated manually against the raw request body, never via Pydantic required-field enforcement), or GET /flashcards/due with section_id but no essay_id — 400 ApiError
NOT_FOUND — GET /essays/{essay_id} with unknown id, or POST .../review with unknown flashcard_id — 404 ApiError

INGESTION_ERROR — the one-shot CLI ingestion script exits non-zero and writes nothing to the database when: YAML front matter is missing or unparsable; title or slug is missing from front matter; a `##` heading lacks the required `{#slug}` anchor suffix; a section contains more than one ```flashcards fenced block; a section has non-blank content after its ```flashcards fenced block; the ```flashcards block is not valid YAML or is missing the top-level `cards` key; any card entry is missing id, q, or a; the same anchor_slug appears twice in one file; the same card id (card_key) appears twice in one file. This is a CLI-local failure mode, not an HTTP response — it has no ApiError shape because ingestion has no HTTP surface.
DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE — Postgres unreachable at startup or during a request — startup logs the error and continues; requests fail until the database is reachable

consumes: psycopg2.pool.SimpleConnectionPool (minconn=1, maxconn=5) via get_db() context manager — RealDictCursor
PyYAML (yaml.safe_load) — used only by the ingestion CLI, never by the HTTP API
provides: CORS: allow_origin_regex=http://localhost:\d+ — all localhost ports during development
backend.ingest — a CLI entrypoint (python -m backend.ingest <path>), not an HTTP surface, run manually by the user after editing the source markdown file

query_behavior.empty_result_behavior: valid — Dataset with rows=[] when no essay has been ingested; UI shows an empty state, not an error
query_behavior.zero_fill_behavior: not applicable — flat list, not a time series

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/essaycards/essays/{essay_id}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Return one essay and its ordered sections, embedded on the single returned row.

query_behavior.ordering: embedded sections ordered by order_index asc
query_behavior.empty_result_behavior: 404 ApiError if essay_id does not exist; an essay with zero sections is valid and returns sections: []

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/essaycards/flashcards/due
exposed_surfaces.purpose: List due flashcards, optionally scoped to one essay or one section within an essay.

params.section_id: optional, uuid, requires essay_id to also be present

query_behavior.defaults: neither param given → all due cards system-wide
query_behavior.allowed_combinations: {}: system-wide; {essay_id}: due cards in that essay; {essay_id, section_id}: due cards in that section only. {section_id only} is rejected with VALIDATION_ERROR.
query_behavior.time_basis: server time — 'due' means next_due_at <= now(), where now() is evaluated by Postgres at query execution time
query_behavior.empty_result_behavior: valid — Dataset with rows=[] when nothing is due for the given scope
query_behavior.zero_fill_behavior: not applicable — flat list, not a time series

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/essaycards/flashcards/{flashcard_id}/review
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Grade a flashcard and persist its updated review-scheduling state using the spaced-repetition formula.
exposed_surfaces.ui_contract: none — mutation endpoint per R-CON-BP-04; returns a typed record { flashcard_id, last_reviewed_at, next_due_at } on success (200), ApiError on failure

body.grade: one of again | hard | good | easy, required. Parsed and validated manually by the handler from the raw JSON request body (not a Pydantic-required field), so every invalid shape — missing grade, non-string grade, out-of-set grade, or unparsable JSON — is caught by application code and returned as ApiError with error.code=VALIDATION_ERROR (400), never FastAPI's default RequestValidationError 422 shape

internal_flow.name: startup_init
internal_flow.description: On FastAPI startup: init_pool() creates the psycopg2 SimpleConnectionPool. init_schema() reads schema.sql and executes DDL idempotently. Errors are logged; the application continues running (requests fail until Postgres is reachable).
outputs: essaycards schema with essays, essay_sections, flashcards, flashcard_review_state tables present

internal_flow.name: ingest_parse
internal_flow.description: backend/ingest.py reads the file at the given path. Parses YAML front matter delimited by a leading '---' line and the next '---' line (yaml.safe_load); requires non-empty title and slug, else aborts. Scans the remaining body line-by-line for `^##\s+(.+?)\s*\{#([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)\}\s*$` to find section boundaries in order of appearance; any `##` heading line that does not match this pattern aborts ingestion citing the line number and heading text. Content before the first matched section heading is discarded (no essay-level intro field exists). For each section, scans its content for a fenced block opened by a line matching `^```flashcards\s*$` and closed by the next line matching `^```\s*$`: zero matches means the section has zero flashcards (body_markdown = full trimmed section content); exactly one match means body_markdown = content before the opening fence (trimmed) and everything after the closing fence must be blank/whitespace-only (else abort); more than one match aborts ('multiple flashcards blocks in one section'). The matched fenced content is parsed as YAML expecting a top-level `cards` list of mappings, each requiring non-empty string keys id, q, a — extra keys are ignored; a missing required key aborts, citing the section anchor_slug and the card's position. Duplicate anchor_slug across sections, or duplicate card id (card_key) across the whole file, aborts ingestion before any database write.
inputs: markdown file at given filesystem path
outputs: in-memory parsed structure: {title, slug, sections: [{heading, anchor_slug, order_index, body_markdown, cards: [{card_key, question, answer}]}]} — or an ingestion abort with a descriptive error and non-zero exit code, no DB writes made

internal_flow.name: ingest_upsert
internal_flow.description: Opens one database transaction. Upserts the essay row keyed by slug (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (slug) DO UPDATE SET title, updated_at). For each section in file order, upserts keyed by (essay_id, anchor_slug) (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET heading, order_index, body_markdown, updated_at). For each card, upserts keyed by (essay_id, card_key) (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET question, answer, section_id, updated_at RETURNING id, created_at, (xmax = 0) AS was_inserted). When was_inserted is true, inserts a matching flashcard_review_state row with last_reviewed_at = null and next_due_at = the returned created_at. When was_inserted is false (an existing card was updated), flashcard_review_state is left completely untouched. Commits on success; rolls back the entire transaction on any database error.
outputs: essay, section, and flashcard rows upserted in Postgres; flashcard_review_state rows created only for newly-inserted flashcards; printed summary of created/updated counts

internal_flow.name: essays_list
internal_flow.description: GET /api/essaycards/essays selects id, title, slug from essaycards.essays ordered by created_at asc. Returns Dataset.

internal_flow.name: essay_detail
internal_flow.description: GET /api/essaycards/essays/{essay_id} fetches the essay row (404 ApiError if missing), then fetches all essay_sections for that essay_id ordered by order_index asc, and embeds them as a `sections` list on the single returned row (list of {id, heading, anchor_slug, order_index, body_markdown}). Returns Dataset (single row).
outputs: Dataset (single row with embedded sections list) | 404 ApiError

internal_flow.name: flashcards_due
internal_flow.description: GET /api/essaycards/flashcards/due validates that section_id is not present without essay_id (400 VALIDATION_ERROR if violated). Joins flashcards to flashcard_review_state, filters WHERE next_due_at <= now() plus any provided essay_id/section_id equality filters, orders by next_due_at asc. Returns Dataset with rows {id, flashcard_id, question, answer, essay_id, section_id, anchor_slug, next_due_at} — anchor_slug is denormalized from essay_sections via join so the client can build the 'Jump to passage' link without a second request.
outputs: Dataset with due flashcard rows | 400 ApiError

internal_flow.name: flashcard_review
internal_flow.description: POST /api/essaycards/flashcards/{flashcard_id}/review reads the raw JSON request body directly (not through a Pydantic body model, so FastAPI's automatic RequestValidationError path is never triggered for this endpoint) and validates manually that a `grade` key is present and is a string one of {again, hard, good, easy}; any other shape — missing key, non-string value, out-of-set value, or an unparsable JSON body — returns 400 ApiError with error.code=VALIDATION_ERROR. Opens a transaction; SELECT now() once to obtain the single authoritative instant for this request. Fetches the flashcard's current flashcard_review_state (404 NOT_FOUND if the flashcard_id does not exist). Calls backend.scheduling.compute_next_due_at(grade, last_reviewed_at, now) which implements the exact floor/doubling formula. UPDATEs flashcard_review_state SET last_reviewed_at = now, next_due_at = computed_value, updated_at = now WHERE flashcard_id = :id. Commits. Returns the typed record {flashcard_id, last_reviewed_at, next_due_at}.

risks.risk: Content before the first `##` section heading in the source file is silently discarded (no essay-level intro/body field exists in this data model)
risks.impact: If an author writes an introductory paragraph before the first heading expecting it to appear in the reader, it will be silently dropped on every ingestion. This is a deliberate Sprint 1 scope decision (the draft's data model has no field to hold it), not an accidental gap — but it should be called out to the content author.

risks.risk: Deletion/reconciliation of sections or flashcards removed from the source file is explicitly out of scope for Sprint 1 (confirmed, per the draft's request) — re-ingestion never deletes essaycards.essay_sections or essaycards.flashcards rows, even when the corresponding heading/card block is removed from the markdown file
risks.impact: If an author deletes a section or a flashcard from the source file and re-ingests, the old row (and, for flashcards, its review state) remains in the database indefinitely: an orphaned flashcard will keep appearing in the due queue and keep accumulating review history for content that no longer exists in the source; an orphaned section will keep appearing in the reader view with its last-ingested body_markdown. There is no cleanup path in Sprint 1 — manual SQL deletion is the only remedy. This is accepted as-is for Sprint 1 per the draft's explicit request, not silently resolved.

risks.risk: The ingestion CLI runs inside the Docker container and needs the source markdown file to be reachable at a container filesystem path
risks.impact: If the compose.yml content volume mount is missed or misconfigured, `docker exec ... python -m backend.ingest <path>` will fail with a file-not-found error rather than a domain-level ingestion error. Deferral to application_implementer covers adding the mount.
